note: Required elements per document type, scored by code from quoted evidence. Bands follow the objective quality scorer (80% and 60%).

checklists.label: Research brief
checklists.basis: Founder's brief rubric (2026-10-18); ISO 20252:2019 research request requirements.

elements.label: Background to the problem
elements.present: The situation, what led to the research and what is already known.
elements.partial: A sentence or two of context without what prompted the research or what is known.
elements.recommendation: Add a short background: the situation, what prompted the research now, and what is already known.

elements.label: Business problem
elements.present: The business problem the research is meant to help solve, stated as a problem.
elements.partial: A topic or area of interest rather than a problem.
elements.recommendation: State the business problem in one or two sentences: what is going wrong or what is unknown, and why it matters.

elements.label: Decision the research informs
elements.present: The decision(s) the results will be used for, and by whom.
elements.partial: Use of the results is implied but no decision is named.
elements.recommendation: Name the decision the research will inform and who will make it.

elements.label: Users of the results
elements.present: Who will receive and act on the findings.
elements.recommendation: Say who will use the results, so the reporting can be shaped for them.

elements.label: At least three research objectives
elements.present: Three or more distinct research objectives.
elements.recommendation: List at least three distinct research objectives, each answerable by the research.

elements.label: Objectives specific and measurable
elements.present: Objectives that say what will be measured, among whom.
elements.partial: Objectives present but vague about what or whom.
elements.recommendation: Rewrite each objective to say what will be measured and among whom.

elements.label: Information needs or hypotheses
elements.present: The specific questions, measures or hypotheses the client needs answered.
elements.partial: General areas of interest without specific questions.
elements.recommendation: List the specific questions or hypotheses each objective must answer.

elements.label: Target population
elements.present: Who the research is about (for example customers, lapsed users, a region).
elements.recommendation: Define the target population: who is in and who is out.

elements.label: Geography and scope
elements.present: Where and over what scope the research applies.
elements.recommendation: State the geography and scope the results must cover.

elements.label: Method requirements or constraints
elements.present: Required or preferred approach, mode or constraints (or an explicit invitation to propose).
elements.partial: A method mentioned without the reason or constraint.
elements.recommendation: Say what method requirements or constraints apply, or invite the agency to propose and justify one.

elements.label: Reporting groups or sample needs
elements.present: Sub-groups the results must be reported for, or sample expectations.
elements.partial: Groups mentioned without the need to report on them.
elements.recommendation: List the sub-groups that results must be reported for, so the sample can be designed for them.

elements.label: Existing data and previous research
elements.present: Previous studies, data or tracking that the research should build on.
elements.partial: Mentioned without saying what it is or how to use it.
elements.recommendation: List previous research and data the agency should review or build on.

elements.label: Deliverables expected
elements.present: The outputs expected (report, deck, data, workshop).
elements.recommendation: List the deliverables you expect and their format.

elements.label: Deadline
elements.present: A date or period by which results are needed.
elements.recommendation: Give the date by which results are needed and any interim milestones.

elements.label: Budget indication
elements.present: A budget, range or cost ceiling.
elements.partial: A statement that budget is limited without a figure or range.
elements.recommendation: Give a budget range or ceiling so proposals can be sized realistically.

checklists.retired: RQK-2 (Grant, 2026-10-19): a brief is now rated on the ten RQC-3 dimensions and their dashboard instead. Kept so reviews scored under RQK-1 still show their checklist.

checklists.label: Research proposal
checklists.basis: Founder's proposal rubric (2026-10-18); ISO 20252:2019 proposal requirements.

elements.label: Restates the business problem
elements.present: The business problem restated accurately (compared with the brief when one is selected).
elements.partial: Restated loosely or differently from the brief.
elements.recommendation: Restate the business problem in your own words and confirm it matches the brief.

elements.label: Restates the objectives
elements.present: The brief's objectives restated, each traceable.
elements.partial: Some objectives restated, others missing or changed.
elements.recommendation: Restate each of the brief's objectives so the client can confirm the scope.

elements.label: Additional or refined objectives
elements.present: Objectives added or sharpened, with the reason.
elements.recommendation: Say which objectives you added or sharpened and why.

elements.label: Relevant literature or prior evidence
elements.present: Relevant previous research, theory or evidence that shapes the approach.
elements.recommendation: Summarise the relevant prior research and how it shapes the design.

elements.label: Research design named and justified
elements.present: The design (for example survey, interviews, experiment, mixed) and why it suits the objectives.
elements.recommendation: Name the research design and explain why it answers the objectives.

elements.label: Data collection method
elements.present: How data will be collected (mode: online, telephone, face to face, interviews).
elements.recommendation: State the data collection mode and why it suits the population.

elements.label: Target population defined
elements.present: Who is eligible, with inclusion and exclusion rules.
elements.recommendation: Define the target population with inclusion and exclusion criteria.

elements.label: Sampling frame or recruitment source
elements.present: Where participants come from (list, panel, database, intercept).
elements.recommendation: Name the sampling frame or recruitment source and its coverage gaps.

elements.label: Sampling method
elements.present: How participants are selected (probability or non-probability, quotas, purposive).
elements.recommendation: State how participants are selected, and whether results can be generalised.

elements.label: Sample size with rationale
elements.present: The sample size and why it is enough for the analysis and sub-groups.
elements.recommendation: Give the sample size and the reasoning (precision, sub-group bases or saturation).

elements.label: Instrument outline
elements.present: What the questionnaire or guide will cover, linked to the objectives.
elements.recommendation: Outline the questionnaire or guide sections and link each to an objective.

elements.label: Pilot or pretest
elements.present: A pilot, cognitive test or soft launch before full fieldwork.
elements.recommendation: Plan a pilot or pretest and say what it will check.

elements.label: Fieldwork quality control
elements.present: Checks on data quality during fieldwork (back-checks, attention checks, supervision).
elements.recommendation: Describe the fieldwork quality checks you will apply.

elements.label: Ethics, consent and data protection
elements.present: Informed consent, confidentiality and data protection (for example POPIA in South Africa).
elements.partial: Mentioned without how it is handled.
elements.recommendation: Say how consent, confidentiality and data protection (POPIA) will be handled.

elements.label: Analysis plan linked to objectives
elements.present: How each objective will be analysed (methods, comparisons, outputs).
elements.recommendation: Set out how each objective will be analysed and what output it produces.

elements.label: Weighting or adjustment
elements.present: Whether and how data will be weighted, or why not.
elements.recommendation: Say whether data will be weighted, to what, and why.

elements.label: Precision and testing
elements.present: Margins of error, significance testing or (for qualitative work) how rigour is ensured.
elements.recommendation: State how precision will be reported or, for qualitative work, how rigour will be shown.

elements.label: Anticipated limitations
elements.present: Known limitations of the design and how they are handled.
elements.recommendation: List the design's limitations and how each will be handled or reported.

elements.label: Products and deliverables
elements.present: The deliverables and their format (compared with the brief when one is selected).
elements.partial: Deliverables listed but not matching the brief.
elements.recommendation: List each deliverable and confirm it meets what the brief asked for.

elements.label: Timeline
elements.present: A schedule with milestones that meets the brief's deadline.
elements.partial: A total duration without milestones, or a timeline that misses the deadline.
elements.recommendation: Give a timeline with milestones and confirm it meets the deadline.

elements.label: Budget
elements.present: A cost, with a breakdown or what is included.
elements.partial: A total without what it covers.
elements.recommendation: Give the cost and what it includes, within the brief's budget.

elements.label: Team and experience
elements.present: Who will do the work and their relevant experience.
elements.recommendation: Name the team and their relevant experience.

checklists.label: Questionnaire
checklists.basis: Krosnick and Presser (2010), Question and questionnaire design; standard pretesting practice.

elements.label: Questions cover every objective
elements.present: Questions that address each research objective.
elements.recommendation: Map each objective to its questions and add questions for any objective not covered.

elements.label: Screening and eligibility
elements.present: Questions that confirm the respondent belongs to the target population.
elements.recommendation: Add screening questions that confirm eligibility before the main questions.

elements.label: Questions for reporting groups
elements.present: Demographic or profile questions needed for the planned sub-group analysis.
elements.recommendation: Add the profile questions needed to report on each sub-group.

elements.label: One idea per question
elements.present: Questions that each ask about one thing (no double-barrelled questions).
elements.partial: One or two questions ask about two things at once.
elements.recommendation: Split any question that asks about two things into separate questions.

elements.label: Neutral wording
elements.present: Questions worded without leading or loaded language.
elements.recommendation: Reword leading questions so they do not suggest an answer.

elements.label: Clear language and defined terms
elements.present: Simple language, with terms defined where needed.
elements.recommendation: Simplify the wording and define any technical terms.

elements.label: Reference periods stated
elements.present: Time frames given for behaviour questions (for example in the past month).
elements.partial: Some behaviour questions without a time frame.
elements.recommendation: Add a reference period to every behaviour question.

elements.label: Options mutually exclusive and exhaustive
elements.present: Answer lists that do not overlap and cover all answers (with Other where needed).
elements.recommendation: Check every answer list for overlap and gaps, and add Other where needed.

elements.label: Balanced, labelled scales
elements.present: Rating scales with balanced, labelled points.
elements.recommendation: Use balanced scales with every point (or at least the ends) labelled.

elements.label: Don't know and not applicable handled
elements.present: Explicit handling of don't know, not applicable or refusal.
elements.recommendation: Decide where don't know or not applicable is offered and apply it consistently.

elements.label: Routing and skip logic
elements.present: Instructions for who answers which questions.
elements.recommendation: Specify routing for every question that does not apply to everyone.

elements.label: Logical order
elements.present: A flow from general to specific, with sensitive questions later.
elements.recommendation: Reorder from general to specific and move sensitive questions later.

elements.label: Introduction and consent
elements.present: An introduction with purpose, duration, confidentiality and consent.
elements.recommendation: Add an introduction covering purpose, length, confidentiality and consent.

elements.label: Estimated length
elements.present: An estimate of how long the questionnaire takes.
elements.recommendation: State the expected interview length and check it against the mode.

checklists.label: Methodology or report
checklists.basis: AAPOR Code of Professional Ethics and Practices (2021), disclosure standards; ISO 20252:2019 reporting requirements.

elements.label: Sponsor and conductor
elements.present: Who commissioned and who conducted the research.
elements.recommendation: State who commissioned and who conducted the research.

elements.label: Fieldwork dates
elements.present: When the data were collected.
elements.recommendation: Give the fieldwork start and end dates.

elements.label: Population studied
elements.present: The population the results describe.
elements.recommendation: Define the population the results describe.

elements.label: Sampling frame and coverage
elements.present: Where the sample came from and who it may miss.
elements.recommendation: Describe the sampling frame and who it may miss.

elements.label: Sample design
elements.present: How the sample was selected (probability or non-probability, quotas, stratification).
elements.recommendation: Describe how the sample was selected, including quotas or stratification.

elements.label: Achieved sample size
elements.present: The number of completed interviews or participants, overall and for key groups.
elements.partial: An overall total without key group bases.
elements.recommendation: Report the achieved sample size overall and for each key group.

elements.label: Data collection mode
elements.present: How data were collected.
elements.recommendation: State the data collection mode(s).

elements.label: Question wording available
elements.present: The questionnaire or exact question wording, or where to find it.
elements.recommendation: Include the questionnaire or the exact wording of questions reported.

elements.label: Response or participation rate
elements.present: The response, cooperation or completion rate, or why it cannot be calculated.
elements.recommendation: Report the response or participation rate and how it was calculated.

elements.label: Weighting
elements.present: Whether and how the data were weighted, and to what targets.
elements.recommendation: Describe the weighting: variables, targets and source.

elements.label: Precision
elements.present: Margins of error or confidence intervals, or (for non-probability samples) why they are not given.
elements.partial: Precision stated without how it was calculated.
elements.recommendation: Report precision with its method, or explain why it does not apply to this sample.

elements.label: Data cleaning and quality checks
elements.present: How the data were checked and cleaned.
elements.recommendation: Describe the quality checks and how cases were excluded.

elements.label: Bases shown for findings
elements.present: The base (number answering) shown for reported figures.
elements.recommendation: Show the base for every reported figure.

elements.label: Claims supported by the data shown
elements.present: Conclusions that follow from the figures reported.
elements.partial: Some claims go beyond the data shown.
elements.recommendation: Check every conclusion against the figures and qualify any that go beyond them.

elements.label: Limitations stated
elements.present: The study's limitations and their effect on the findings.
elements.recommendation: State the limitations and how they affect the findings.

elements.label: Findings linked to objectives
elements.present: Findings organised by, or traced to, the research objectives.
elements.recommendation: Show how each objective is answered, and say which could not be.

elements.label: Recommendations follow from findings
elements.present: Recommendations traced to the findings that support them.
elements.recommendation: Link each recommendation to the findings that support it.
